effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` USDC to the vault, using the signer's USDC allowance to the vault (safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
onBehalf receives newly minted roxNUVA shares, in the amount previewDeposit(assets) gives after interest and fees accrue; no minimum is enforced.
The vault may move the deposited USDC to its liquidity adapter. This does not change the signer's position.
formats.shown: Deposit 50000 USDC for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker roxNUVA and 'Send shares to' <onBehalf>; the number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many roxNUVA shares the signer receives; the share price sets it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);` The function has no minimum-shares parameter. Case 0: the signer receives 49861.337 roxNUVA and the screen shows no share amount.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The amount comes from storage. A label such as 'Shares sent to' already names the asset and the party.

findings.title: deposit labels the amount 'Deposit asset' and shows the share ticker as a separate raw constant field.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit fields: `"label": "Deposit asset"` on `assets` (tokenAmount), and `{"label": "Share ticker", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker"}`.
findings.fix: Rename the label to 'Deposit amount'. Merge the ticker into the recipient label, for example 'roxNUVA shares to'.

cases.notes: The screen shows 50000 USDC out right. It names roxNUVA shares and the recipient, but not the share amount (49861.34). The reader got the direction and the asset but not the amount.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns roxNUVA shares from onBehalf, in the amount previewWithdraw(assets) gives (rounded up); no maximum is enforced.
receiver receives exactly `assets` USDC from the vault.
When the signer is not onBehalf, the call spends the signer's roxNUVA share allowance from onBehalf by the number of shares burned.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 100000 USDC to <receiver>, with Owner <onBehalf>; the number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw does not show how many roxNUVA shares it burns from the owner; the share price sets it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`. exit: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares);`. Case 1: 99737.70 roxNUVA leave the signer, and the screen shows only 'Withdraw exactly 100000 USDC'.
findings.fix: None for the amount. You can change the 'Owner' label to 'Burn roxNUVA shares of' to name the asset that leaves.

cases.notes: The screen shows 100000 USDC in to the signer right. It shows the share burn only through the 'Owner' field, without the asset or the amount. The reader guessed that shares are reduced.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` roxNUVA from onBehalf.
receiver receives USDC in the amount previewRedeem(shares) gives (rounded down); no minimum is enforced.
When the signer is not onBehalf, the call spends the signer's roxNUVA share allowance from onBehalf by `shares`.
formats.shown: Redeem 997.77 roxNUVA to <receiver>, with Owner <onBehalf>; nothing says that USDC is the asset received or how much arrives.

findings.title: redeem never names USDC as the asset the receiver gets; the screen shows only the shares.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = USDC (constructor _asset 0xA0b8...eB48). The redeem format has no field that uses underlyingToken. Case 2: the signer receives 1000.000380 USDC. Reader: 'the screen does not say which asset or how much'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field `{"label": "Receive asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}`. Or change interpolatedIntent to 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem cannot show how much USDC arrives; the share price sets it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. The function has no minimum-assets parameter. Case 2: 1000.000380 USDC arrives, and no amount or bound is shown.

cases.notes: The screen shows the 997.77 roxNUVA burn right. The screen names neither the asset (USDC) nor the amount of the USDC that arrives. The reader knew only that something arrives.
